notes: A clean generic isUnquoted helper applied consistently, including the `{}` case, with an insightful snippet-placeholder test; it misses the address HasSuffix check and adds a formatter test for code it never changed.

A generic `isUnquoted(text)` helper is applied at every structural brace site and also fixes the quoted `{}` branch like the reference; it misses the quoted-address HasSuffix tweak, but the tests are thorough, including the snippet placeholder regression case.

Covers every site the reference touches, including the address HasSuffix check and the `{}` branch; the repeated inline `!Quoted()` checks and the now-redundant `wasQuoted == 0` leftovers in directive() are less clean than a helper.

Inline `Quoted()` checks cover all sites, including HasSuffix and the `{}` branch, so it is the most complete relative to the reference, though slightly repetitive in doImport; it adds solid parser and dispenser tests plus an integration adapt test.

Correct fix with inline quoted checks, cleaned-up directive() logic and strong tests (named routes, snippets, unbalanced quoted brace), but it misses the quoted-address HasSuffix check that the reference adjusts.

Inline `!Quoted()` checks at every structural brace site (including the `{}` branch and the doImport switch) fix the issue correctly but are repetitive; it skips the address HasSuffix case, and its tests are good, covering named routes, snippets, unbalanced quoted braces and the adapter.

Nearly matches the reference using clean Token helper methods and has thorough parser, dispenser and adapter tests; only a redundant wasQuoted check remains and the pre-existing quoted-`{}` branch quirk is left alone.

Adds clean Token helper methods and updates every brace check in the dispenser and parser, including the quoted-address HasSuffix check; it leaves the `"{}"` branch in directive() matching quoted tokens (a minor, pre-existing edge), and its tests cover parser, dispenser and adapter.

Matches the reference: returns every import block, deduplicates by concrete instance in expandResourceImports, and adds apply tests covering the basic case, parent/child per-instance override, and a for_each child import.

Matches the reference: it returns every import statement and dedups per resource instance during expansion, so a parent block wins only for the exact instance it targets; its three apply tests cover the root case, a static child override, and a for_each child override.

Fixes the reported same-module for_each case by keeping all blocks from one module, but parent-overrides-child still works per whole resource, so a parent block targeting `foo["a"]` silently drops the child's import of `foo["b"]` (the same silent-drop bug across modules; 2 of 3 hidden tests fail).

Takes essentially the same per-module claiming approach as C2, so it fixes the root-module scenario but still discards a child's imports for unrelated instances when a parent targets any instance; it adds only a single basic regression test.

Statically parses `to` addresses to find per-instance conflicts, which is brittle: any dynamic (for_each) child import block is treated as conflicting and dropped entirely, and keyed-module addresses can slip past it; it also adds unrelated child-sorting and much more complexity than deferring dedup to expansion.

Statically parses `to` expressions to dedup per instance, which handles literal targets, but it drops an entire dynamic (for_each) child block whenever the parent targets the same resource, may let a child overwrite a parent under keyed modules because no expansion-time dedup is added, and adds parsing complexity in the wrong layer.

Same claimed-by-module approach as C1, with better tests (count and for_each plan test, refactoring unit test), but it keeps the coarse resource-level parent override and silently drops child imports of other instances (fails 2 of 3 hidden tests).

Fixes the reported same-module case, but it keeps the parent override at the whole-resource level, so a parent import of one instance still silently drops a child's imports for other instances (the same silent-drop bug across modules), and its unit-test fixture enshrines that coarse behavior.
